key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can act as a universal, non-contact defect fingerprinting tool for organic halide perovskite solar-cell thin films by linking specific terahertz absorptions to grain-boundary defect species.
engineering_relevance: This enables quantitative defect metrology and feedback-guided passivation, supporting closed-loop quality control to improve perovskite device reliability and efficiency.
method: Measured THz-TDS spectra (0.3–3.0 THz) of four sequential vacuum evaporation perovskites: MAPbI3, MAPbBr3, FAPbI3, and CsPbI3.
Identified intrinsic phonon modes and grain-boundary-localized molecular defect vibrations as material-specific fingerprints.
Used oscillator-strength analysis to correlate the 1.58 THz MAPbI3 absorption with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a linear scaling between THz oscillator strength and XPS-measured defect concentration, supporting THz-TDS as a direct quantitative defect meter.
watch_item: The approach depends on a well-built reference THz fingerprint library and may need careful calibration to separate overlapping defect and phonon signals in real device stacks.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
